It is at least reasonably possible that the estimated range of the loss will change in the near term as additional information from the Court is made available.

The amendment also modified the interest rate to be calculated at a floating rate per month equal to (a) the greater of (i) 8.25 % per year (previously 3.25 % per year) or (ii) the Prime Rate published by The Wall Street Journal, or such other rate of interest publicly announced by the Lender as its Prime Rate, plus (b) 1.00 % (previously 1.50 %), plus an additional 5.00 % during any period that an event of default has occurred and is continuing.

In addition, the amendment modified certain financial covenants, including (a) the amount of the Borrowers’ cash maintained at Lender (b) revising how quick ratio is calculated for purposes of the quick ratio covenant, and (c) Borrowers’ minimum liquidity requirements.

If the Company draws from the line of credit, the Company’s obligations under the Credit Agreement are secured by a security interest in substantially all of the Company’s current and future personal property assets, including intellectual property. Any borrowings, interest or other fees or obligations that the Company owes will become due and payable on the maturity date. The Credit Agreement includes quick ratio financial covenants. If the Company draws from the line of credit, the Company is also subject to a number of affirmative and restrictive covenants, including covenants regarding delivery of financial statements, the amount of the Company’s cash maintained at Western Alliance Bank, maintenance of inventory, payment of taxes, maintenance of insurance, dispositions of property, business combinations or acquisitions and incurrence of additional indebtedness, among other customary covenants. As the Company had no borrowings under the line of credit as of December 31, 2023, the Company was not subject to the covenants of this agreement.

payload.fact: Has the D. Del. (1:18-cv-01434) fixed the amount of Elysium's attorney fee and cost award against ChromaDex, and if so, what is the amount? Will ChromaDex secure it pending appeal with cash collateral, a surety bond (and on what collateral terms) or a letter of credit, and how much of its cash would be locked or paid before Nov 20, 2024?
payload.why_pivotal: This decides whether the requested structure passes once the dispute is counted. If the ~$9.8M ceiling is bonded with cash collateral, lowest projected cash falls to ~$12.7M and the order limit drops to ~$1.43M, below the $2.0M request. With the bank data alone, the $2.0M inst_90 request passes (order limit ~$2.72M).
payload.acceptable_evidence: D. Del. order on the amount of fees and costs; ChromaDex 8-K or management confirmation of the supersedeas bond/collateral arrangements; surety bond terms showing any cash collateral requirement
payload.if_resolved: If no ruling is expected within the horizon, or the award is secured by a surety bond with little cash collateral, or the amount is materially below $9.8M, the $2.0M inst_90 structure passes on the event-adjusted view (subject to exception review). If the ~$9.8M is paid, or secured with full cash collateral, within the horizon, cap the order at about $1.43M (inst_90_1430000) or decline the excess.

payload.fact: Do the Western Alliance Bank Credit Agreement covenants (quick ratio, minimum liquidity, cash at lender, and any indebtedness or negative-pledge covenant in the Dec 2023 amendment) permit ChromaDex to incur $2.0M of unsecured Slope bill-pay financing, or is lender consent required?
payload.why_pivotal: Slope policy requires existing lenders' covenants to permit the financing. The public summaries say the additional-indebtedness covenant applies only when the line is drawn and that the quick ratio covenant exists, but not whether trade financing is permitted indebtedness.
payload.acceptable_evidence: Text of the Credit Agreement and the fifth amendment (8-K Exhibit 10.2), or written confirmation or consent from Western Alliance Bank
payload.if_resolved: If it is permitted, or consent is given, there is no further condition. If it is not permitted, decline until the lender consents.

payload.fact: Has Elysium paid the $2,500,000 ordered by the C.D. Cal. final judgment of Aug 13, 2024, and on what date?
payload.why_pivotal: Receipt would raise projected cash by $2.5M and partly offset a fee-award collateral lock. The stress path that binds the event-adjusted limit assumes it is not collected within the horizon.
payload.acceptable_evidence: Connected-bank data showing the receipt, or a ChromaDex disclosure
payload.if_resolved: If received, it enters the connected-bank data and the next review, and the event-adjusted order limit rises. If not received, the decision stands on the paths where it is uncollected.

payload.summary: ChromaDex requests Slope bill-pay financing of a $2.0M contract-manufacturer invoice on 3 monthly installments (inst_90), funded 2024-08-20. Tier A. Bank-only view: limit $3.62M and order limit $2.72M, so the request passes. Two live Elysium matters were placed on the dispute model. (1) C.D. Cal. 8:16-cv-02277 final judgment of 2024-08-13 (fnd_001): Elysium must pay ChromaDex $2,500,000, each side bears its own fees, and appeals are barred. ChromaDex is the creditor; receipt is not yet evidenced (eff_009). (2) D. Del. 1:18-cv-01434: fee motion granted 2024-03-25 and amount fully briefed and pending (fnd_002). ChromaDex intends to appeal, has not accrued a liability, and estimates exposure at about $9.8M including post-judgment interest (fnd_003; eff_008, no current cash). The Western Alliance $10.0M revolver is undrawn (fnd_004, fnd_005). It is treated as a funding condition, not as cash (eff_006). Event-adjusted view: the binding stress path (fee award bonded with the model's cash collateral lock while the $2.5M is uncollected) takes lowest projected cash to about $12.7M on 2025-02-15. That sets the order limit at about $1.43M, so the $2.0M request fails and inst_90_1430000 is the largest passing structure. The $9.8M used is ChromaDex's own ceiling estimate, not a court-fixed amount. No settlement effects exist, so sensitivity was not applicable.

Whether the Western Alliance Bank Credit Agreement covenants permit $2.0M of unsecured Slope financing or require lender consent (fact_002)
Date on which Elysium pays the $2.5M C.D. Cal. judgment (fact_003)
payload.conclusion: On bank data alone, the $2.0M 90-day installment request passes (order limit about $2.72M). Once the Elysium disputes are counted, it does not: the event-adjusted order limit is about $1.43M. That limit is bound by a stress path in which ChromaDex secures the pending Delaware attorney-fee award (up to about $9.8M including interest, per its 10-Q estimate) with cash collateral pending appeal, and the $2.5M California judgment receivable has not yet been collected. Recommendation: route to exception review (material litigation; existing secured lender). Offer at most about $1.43M on inst_90 (inst_90_1430000) unless evidence shows the fee award will not lock or consume that cash within the horizon. Conditions: (a) confirm the fee amount and whether appeal security is cash-collateralised; (b) confirm Western Alliance Bank's covenants permit the financing, or obtain consent; (c) count the $2.5M from Elysium only once received. The fee amount and appeal security are the pivotal unknowns. The path weights are model judgment, not default probabilities.
